Fine-Gray competing-risk regression

Source: R/competing_risk_reg.R
competing_risk_reg.Rd

Fit proportional subdistribution hazards models and return publication-ready subdistribution hazard ratios.

Usage

competing_risk_reg(
  data,
  time,
  event,
  event_of_interest,
  exposures,
  censor_code = 0,
  adjust_for = NULL,
  multivariable = FALSE,
  multivariate = NULL,
  format = c("flextable", "gt"),
  theme = c("minimal"),
  model_stats = FALSE,
  show_ref = TRUE
)

Arguments

data

A data frame containing follow-up time, event status, and model variables.

time

Numeric follow-up-time variable. Quoted and bare names work.

event

Event-status variable with one censoring code and distinct codes for the event of interest and competing events.

event_of_interest

Observed code or label for the event being modelled.

exposures

Variables whose effects are reported.

censor_code

Observed code or label for censoring. Defaults to `0`.

adjust_for

Optional adjustment variables. One adjusted model is fitted per exposure and only that exposure is reported.

multivariable

Logical; fit one model containing and reporting all variables in `exposures`.

multivariate

Optional alias for `multivariable`.

format

Output table format: `"flextable"` or `"gt"`.

theme

Table styling preset.

model_stats

Logical; return N, event counts, pseudo-log-likelihood, and convergence status.

show_ref

Logical; display categorical reference rows.

Value

A `gtregression` object containing the publication table, numeric estimates, fitted `crr` models, model summaries, and analysis metadata.

Details

Each model uses the rows that are complete for its own variables. The N column and the footnote report the observations and the events of interest used by the fitted models, with the same wording as cox_reg() and surv_reg().

Fine-Gray regression models the subdistribution hazard for the selected event. An SHR above 1 indicates a higher cumulative incidence of that event over follow-up, accounting for the presence of competing events. It is not a cause-specific Cox hazard ratio and should not be interpreted as one.

Examples

competing_risk_reg(
  data_competing_risk,
  time = follow_up_months,
  event = outcome,
  event_of_interest = Relapse,
  censor_code = Censored,
  exposures = c(treatment, age, stage)
)
